P.P1_bottleneck_analysis: NSOPW query latency (30s typical). Criminal background query latency (30-60s typical). False positives from name matching (common names). Re-check frequency (annual? never?). Privacy concerns (storing check results).
P.P2_defensibility: NSOPW is official source (legal authority). Criminal background is standard practice. Vendor (Checkr/GoodHire) handles FCRA compliance. Clear pass/fail results (no detailed findings stored).
P.P3_confidence_level: Very high confidence. NSOPW is definitive. Criminal background is standard due diligence. Vendor handles compliance.
P4_failure_modes: NSOPW API down → cannot check (mitigate: queue for later, timeout)
False positive (name match wrong person) → legitimate user flagged (mitigate: manual review, right to dispute)
Criminal record from 30 years ago → user flagged (mitigate: policy: violent crimes only, or time limit)
Re-check never done → user status stale (mitigate: annual re-check job, user-initiated update)
Check result leaked → privacy violation (mitigate: encrypt, strict access control)
P.P5_backup_plan: If check unavailable: queue for later retry. If flag: manual review required. If error: timeout and allow retry or manual review.
P.P6_backup_plan_test: Simulate API failures. Test name matching edge cases (John Smith vs Jon Smith). Test criminal record filtering (old vs recent). Test re-check job. Test encryption of results.
P.P7_testing_strategy: Unit tests for result interpretation (flag vs clear logic). Integration tests with NSOPW (sandbox). Integration tests with vendor (Checkr/GoodHire). Load tests for concurrent checks. Re-check job testing (daily job runs, records updated). Privacy tests (verify encryption).
P.P8_benchmarks: NSOPW query: <30s. Criminal background query: <60s. Total check: <90s. False positive rate: <5% (name collisions). Clear rate: 95%+ (assuming normal population). Re-check job: runs daily, completes within 1 hour.

CH1_change_log.description: Initial CONFolder for background check module

L.L1_legal_considerations: Background checks are subject to Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) if used to make adverse decisions. Must provide user with opportunity to dispute. Cannot use criminal records >7 years old (fair chance rules, some states). Sex offender registry is public but subject to state rules. Vendor (Checkr/GoodHire) must be FCRA-compliant.
L2_regulatory_frameworks: State fair chance laws (criminal record age limits)
L.L3_consent_requirements: Explicit written consent for background check (FCRA requirement). Adverse action notice if flagged. Right to dispute.
L.L4_liability_notes: False positive (legitimate user flagged) could cause harm (loss of trust). Mitigation: right to dispute, manual review. False negative (criminal accepted) enables harm. Mitigation: accurate NSOPW query, vendor reputation. Discrimination risk (using old criminal records). Mitigation: fair chance policy (age limit on records), no race/gender-based decisions. Privacy breach (check results leaked). Mitigation: encryption, access control.

F.F1_cost_considerations: Checkr/GoodHire: ~$20-50 per background check. At 10k users: $200k-500k. NSOPW is free (public API). Annual re-checks: additional cost.
F.F2_accounting_considerations: Per-user cost at signup + annual re-check cost. Budget $50k/year for 10k users. Scale with growth.
F.F3_revenue_impact: Background check enables trust and verified badge (retention driver). Essential for community safety (brand value).

S.S1_cybersecurity: Check results encrypted at rest (AES-256). API calls over TLS. Check results not logged in detail (FCRA compliance). User's identity not re-checked if no address change (reduce cost and privacy exposure).
S.S2_data_privacy: Detailed findings not stored (FCRA compliance). Only pass/fail result stored. User can request deletion (GDPR, CCPA). Re-check frequency limited (annual, not per-login).
S.S3_encryption_requirements: Check result encrypted at rest. Vendor API calls over TLS. Identity data encrypted before sending to vendor.
S.S4_access_control: User sees own check result (pass/fail). Admin sees check result (pass/fail) but not detailed findings. Vendor sees only what's needed (name, DOB, address).
S.S5_audit_requirements: Log all check requests (for FCRA compliance). Log check results (anonymized). Log re-checks. Audit trail retention: 7 years (FCRA requirement).

X.X1_notes: Background checks are critical for community safety and trust. NSOPW is official authoritative source. Vendor (Checkr/GoodHire) handles FCRA compliance. Fair chance rules important (don't discriminate based on old records). Annual re-checks keep status current.
X2_open_questions: Vendor: Checkr, GoodHire, or direct NSOPW? (Checkr/GoodHire add cost but handle compliance)
Criminal record age limit: 7 years, 10 years, no limit? (fair chance policy)
Re-check frequency: annual, never, on-demand? (annual keeps current, adds cost)
What about civil infractions (DUI, drug, disorderly conduct)? (only sex offenses or broader?)
X.X3_related_research: FCRA compliance guidelines. NSOPW documentation. Checkr/GoodHire APIs. Fair chance laws. State sex offender registry rules. Criminal record expungement policies.
